question: What will be the atomicity of oxygen and phosphorous?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Diatomic and tetra-atomic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxygen (O₂)** is a diatomic molecule, meaning it consists of two oxygen atoms.
 
• The diatomic nature of oxygen is due to its tendency to form a double bond (O=O) with another oxygen atom, creating a stable molecule.
 
• **Phosphorus (P₄)**, on the other hand, typically exists as a tetra-atomic molecule, meaning it consists of four phosphorus atoms.
 
• The most common form of phosphorus in nature is white phosphorus, which has a tetrahedral structure with four phosphorus atoms.
 
• The tetra-atomic nature of phosphorus is due to its preference for forming a P₄ molecule to achieve stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diatomic**__

 __
 
• A **diatomic molecule** consists of two atoms of the same element or different elements bonded together.
 
• Examples include **hydrogen (H₂), nitrogen (N₂), and chlorine (Cl₂)**.
 
 
 
• **Tetra-atomic**__
 
 
• A **tetra-atomic molecule** consists of four atoms, which can be either of the same element or different elements.
 
• Examples include **white phosphorus (P₄), arsenic (As₄), and some silicates (SiO₄)**.
